about: The single register of owner decisions that this revision leaves open. Every entry is pending: nothing here is selected, and no operating default is implied. A recommendation is advice only. Sheets, records and notes link here with a dashed Pending tag. Sources: review/claude-architecture-feedback-response.md and review/claude-architecture-feedback-followup.md.

decisions.title: Compensation by other lights while a hold is open
decisions.question: When a person holds one light, may other lights change to make up for it, and how?

options.label: Pin only
options.effect: Free light re-serves everyone, the changer's own region included, so the change can be partly or fully offset there.

options.label: Direction-aware footprint bound
options.effect: Free light may not move against the person's change at the points it moved. Others in the footprint can stay hold-limited for the hold's lifetime.

options.label: Soft penalty
options.effect: A penalty with weight λ_h discourages compensation; partial, with no guarantee either way.

options.label: Changer-aware bound
options.effect: P1's bound only at the changer's own task points; others may be re-served. Needs a reliable changer identity.

sub_choices: P1, P2 and P3 each take a strict or mode form: in mode form, den_lighting's mode transitions (vacancy-off, arrival, game entry, game-time vacancy and return, game exit) sit outside the bound.
P3's fallback for an unknown or uncertain changer: P1 or P0.
parameters: membership rule for shares near the threshold

recommendation.note: For rung-9 replay only: P1 in mode form, with P0 and P3 scored as counterfactual scenes on the same evenings. Choose the canary's option from that report. Advice, not a selection.

decisions.blocks: The coordinator's hold-aware solve beyond pinning (A9 K16), the expected results of the rung-9 hold fixtures, and any canary.

decisions.title: A person's held light against a hard comfort constraint
decisions.question: When light a person holds breaks a hard glare or body-envelope constraint, which wins?

options.label: Manual wins, flagged
options.effect: The held light stays as set; the hard conflict is logged; it never triggers rollback.

options.label: Hard constraint wins
options.effect: K17 dims or switches off the held light (or fades a beam out, keeping its aim), logs a safety override and gives notice.

options.label: Owner-approved exceptions
options.effect: As S0 inside a pre-approved exception (fixture × look × whose envelope), as S1 outside.

sub_choices: S1a restores the person's setting when the conflict clears; S1b keeps it limited until the hold ends.
Decided separately for today's Hue path and before any gimbal admission (E9).

recommendation.note: S0 with the conflict log on today's Hue path; S1 with S2 exceptions before E9. Advice, not a selection.

decisions.blocks: Rollback semantics for held-light conflicts, the safety-override path in K17 and A11, and engineered-fixture admission.

decisions.title: A person's change to a spot that is moving
decisions.question: If a person changes an engineered spot mid-move, does the move stop or finish dark?

options.label: Stop
options.effect: Stop within the fixture's declared stop bound.

options.label: Finish dark
options.effect: Let a move already sent finish dark, if the change names no aim and the end aim still clears the envelope checks; otherwise stop.

recommendation.note: M1 when the change names an aim, M2 otherwise. Advice, not a selection.

decisions.blocks: The engineered-fixture execution sequence (A9 K17, aim while dark). No effect on today's Hue bulbs, which have no aim.

decisions.title: Fields a person's change did not set
decisions.question: When a hold is taken during a system fade, where do the fields the person did not set come from?

options.label: Current actual state
options.effect: As den_lighting does today.

options.label: State before the system fade
options.effect: Restores what the light was before the fade began.

recommendation.note: For parity with den_lighting. Advice, not a selection.

decisions.blocks: The exact held value in a mid-fade change (cases V9d, V9e).

decisions.title: Corrections made while a decision is still being carried out
decisions.question: Does a change during an unfinished step teach anything?

options.label: Judge against the decision's intent
options.effect: Run the attribution order against the requested scene and recipients.

options.label: Abstain
options.effect: AR11 with reason mid_execution; nothing learned. The comfort test is never skipped.

recommendation.note: Advice, not a selection.

decisions.blocks: Attribution of corrections made during a running decision (A11).

decisions.title: A person's "on" for a spot whose aim is unknown
decisions.question: When a stopped spot's aim is unknown and a person turns it on, what happens?

options.label: Apply at once, flagged
options.effect: Lights at an unknown aim; its prediction and verify are unknown.

options.label: Apply after a dark move
options.effect: Moves dark to the last read-back aim, then lights.

options.label: Refuse and say why
options.effect: The spot stays off.

recommendation.note: No recommendation.

decisions.blocks: The engineered-fixture command path after a stop without position readback (case V9k).

decisions.title: Completing a step on the Pi after a change elsewhere
decisions.question: May K17 run the fresh hold and envelope checks itself, on the Pi, to complete a remaining step?

options.label: Allowed, with a local checker
options.effect: K17 holds the new hold's footprint, basis rows and current person states, and completes a step that passes.

options.label: Not allowed
options.effect: Every step that needs fresh checks waits for K16's re-solve.

recommendation.note: Until a local checker exists. Advice, not a selection. Either way a check that cannot run fails closed.

decisions.blocks: Completing a step after an unrelated revision change without a K16 re-solve (cases V8, V9f, V9g).

decisions.title: How long K17 waits for a fresh plan
decisions.question: After a decision is superseded or cut short, how long may K16's re-solve take before the current state is kept?

options.label: Set a deadline D
options.effect: A fresh plan arriving within D is sent under the step check; otherwise kept_current is logged.

recommendation.note: No value proposed.

decisions.blocks: The kept_current outcome's timing.

decisions.title: Keeping a beam whose envelope check fails only through age growth
decisions.question: May a current narrow beam be kept for a time after its conservative envelope check fails only because evidence aged?

options.label: Admit a τ_keep exception
options.effect: Keep the beam for τ_keep from its first failure, logged as hard_conflicts[{constraint: envelope_age}]; counts for rollback unless exempted. Never for a coasting or ambiguous track.

options.label: No exception
options.effect: The hard constraint applies as written: the beam fades out at its first failure.

recommendation.note: No recommendation. Under exception, a free beam whose conservative envelope check fails only through age growth is kept for at most τ_keep from its first failure, logged as hard_conflicts envelope_age; under none it fades out at its first failure. Which applies is the owner's decision.

decisions.blocks: Any kept-beam behaviour under stale geometry (cases V33, V34).

decisions.title: How fresh support reaches the coordinator
decisions.question: Does K16 refresh person evidence before committing or keeping a narrow beam?

options.label: No refresh
options.effect: Use the latest record; sound but wide (a head can be about 7 s old at settle with 10 s heartbeats).

options.label: Refresh before commit
options.effect: Get a current record, or short-cadence support, before committing or keeping a narrow beam near a person.

options.label: Monitored bound
options.effect: A reaction-based bound for observed or deadband-confirmed fields only, given declared emission, gap, liveness and reaction guarantees. Held fields never get it.

recommendation.note: Advice, not a selection. FR2 is also a safety-margin choice (see manual-vs-safety).

decisions.blocks: The effective age term for a beam near a person; whether F2's spot survives in case V33.

decisions.title: Body-envelope seeds, margins and references
decisions.question: What sizes, speeds, deadbands and margins does body-envelope/v1 use, and how are they validated?

options.label: Set and pre-register values
options.effect: Values are fixed before any containment test and validated against independent head and shoulder references.

parameters: v_pos or the Track motion model

recommendation.note: No values proposed. Only the working region's 0.10 m deadband exists today.

decisions.blocks: Whether any narrow beam near a person is feasible; the walkthrough aim's survival.

decisions.title: How delivered service is scored over the evaluation region
decisions.question: Area share above the floor, or the mean over the region?

options.label: Area share
options.effect: The share of valid pixels in R_eval at or above F(c) must reach a_min.

options.label: Mean
options.effect: The mean over valid pixels of R_eval must reach F(c); can pass a bright spot on part of the patch.

recommendation.note: No recommendation.

decisions.blocks: Delivered-service outcomes under partial overlap (case V54).

decisions.title: Missing or uncertain reference geometry
decisions.question: How are need seconds without a usable owner mark treated, and how precise must a mark be?

options.label: Strict
options.effect: Those seconds are unknown for every outcome.

options.label: Bounded
options.effect: As strict, plus a never-gated missed (bounded) column where the whole gold surface is below F(c).

recommendation.note: Advice, not a selection.

decisions.blocks: Service claims on unmarked or uncertain intervals (cases V55, V56).

decisions.title: Adequacy floors and the quiet window
decisions.question: What light is enough for each demand class, and how long must it stand uncorrected?

options.label: Set and pre-register
options.effect: Floors and window fixed before held-out scoring.

recommendation.note: A9's guidance values (for example 500 lx for fine work) are seeds marked Target · validate, not chosen floors. Predicted service is reported in its own column and never gated; that is agreed design, not a parameter.

decisions.blocks: Every served, missed and TTGL outcome.

decisions.title: Promotion margins and the interval convention
decisions.question: What margin δ does each metric get, and is the interval two-sided 95%?

options.label: Two-sided 95% interval
options.effect: One-sided error 2.5% per metric; matches EvalRecord.intervals.

options.label: One-sided 95% interval
options.effect: More power on small gold sets; needs a second interval in the record.

parameters: δ per metric (absolute, in the metric's unit)

recommendation.note: Advice, not a selection. No δ is set.

decisions.blocks: Every non-inferiority and superiority gate (A13 Gate 1, A8, rungs).

decisions.title: Demand bands, competence floors and sample gates
decisions.question: Where do the demand bands start, and what competence and coverage must a demand estimate show?

options.label: Set and pre-register
options.effect: Cut points, floors and per-band sample gates fixed on development data before held-out scoring.

recommendation.note: Tie the fine cut to the task look's trigger (cooking@1 at 0.6) is a candidate. Advice, not a selection. Counting an abstention or a stale answer as a miss is agreed design (F08), not part of this decision.

decisions.blocks: Demand competence at rung 6 and N2, and the A8 student gate.

decisions.title: The onset definition and the entry dwell
decisions.question: What is the gold onset, which system state is timed, and what entry dwell does K7 use?

options.label: Fix before labelling
options.effect: The protocol states the onset, the timed state and T_enter before any label is made.

recommendation.note: Today A7's 5 s entry dwell cannot meet a 3 s first-contact target. Do not shorten the dwell or move labels to make the example pass.

decisions.blocks: The onset gate at rung 6 and in the early need test (N2).

decisions.title: When the early need test runs
decisions.question: Does the one-person need test (N1, N2) run before the tracker is built, and on which retained sessions?

options.label: Before the tracker
options.effect: N1 and N2 run on retained one-person sessions before rungs 1–5 start; a not-feasible verdict reshapes the perception track early.

options.label: Alongside the perception rungs
options.effect: Rungs 1–5 proceed while N1 and N2 are labelled and scored; their verdict arrives later.

options.label: After rung 5
options.effect: The need test runs on real bundles only, with real timing; nothing is learned about the premise before the tracker exists.

recommendation.note: Advice, not a selection: it tests the riskiest premise cheaply. The light track keeps its value whatever it finds.

decisions.blocks: Where N1 and N2 sit on the ladder, and whether rungs 1–5 wait for their verdict.

decisions.title: Recipient and attribution thresholds
decisions.question: What share makes a person a recipient, what change counts as affecting a target, and what precision admits each learning path?

options.label: Set and pre-register
options.effect: Fixed before E1 is scored.

recommendation.note: No values proposed.

decisions.blocks: whose_light classification and every attribution learning path (A11, rung 12).

decisions.title: Game time: ownership and comparison strata
decisions.question: Does the coordinator ever own game time, and how is the first canary stratified?

options.label: Non-gaming strata with handback
options.effect: den_lighting owns the bulbs during games in both arms; game time leaves the comparison.

options.label: Complete policy
options.effect: The candidate reproduces gaming as an externally signalled mode, with the game-exit snapshot restore.

recommendation.note: For the first canary. A complete-policy comparison is needed before any permanent handover. Advice, not a selection.

decisions.blocks: The rung-11 canary design and any claim about game time.

decisions.title: Changing the hold lifetime
decisions.question: Should a hold end with the person's episode instead of den_lighting's vacancy and game rules?

options.label: Keep den_lighting's lifetime
options.effect: Outside a game, until 120 s after the later of vacancy start and the latest touch; during a game, the game's end (game-time vacancy turns held bulbs off without ending the hold); or resume_automatic.

options.label: Episode-based end
options.effect: End with the served episode once engagement offset and tracking are qualified.

recommendation.note: This revision describes den_lighting's lifetime as today's rule; a change is the owner's. Advice, not a selection.

decisions.blocks: Any change to how long a manual setting lasts.

decisions.title: Manual levels becoming the normal scene
decisions.question: Under the coordinator, does a manual level keep becoming the bulb's normal and arrival level, as den_lighting does outside a game?

options.label: Keep den_lighting's behaviour
options.effect: A non-gaming manual write becomes that bulb's normal.

options.label: Stop
options.effect: Arrival levels come from the look and preferences only.

recommendation.note: No recommendation.

decisions.blocks: Arrival behaviour under the coordinator, and whether a pre-game held value returns as normal.

decisions.title: Comfort learning, reports and glare-model validation
decisions.question: How near the glare limit counts, how comfort limits tighten, whether people can report glare, and whether the glare model is validated under supervision?

options.label: Set and pre-register
options.effect: Margin, step and repeat count fixed on development data; reports and validation chosen explicitly.

parameters: explicit glare report channel (app, voice, none)

recommendation.note: Comfort limits only ever tighten from corrections; loosening needs supervised validation or the owner. That rule is part of the agreed design, not this choice.

decisions.blocks: AR10's plausibility test and every comfort-limit update (A11, rung 12).

decisions.title: Absolute light commissioning
decisions.question: Is the grey-card and lux-meter pass acceptable, with which meter, what held-out tolerance, and one scale or one per illuminant class?

options.label: Card and meter pass
options.effect: k_L from a grey card and a meter reading; held-out checks in lux.

options.label: Meter-only per-surface factors
options.effect: Avoids the card; cannot give reflectance for bounce or unmetered surfaces.

options.label: A separately approved sensor
options.effect: If camera photometry fails.

parameters: k_L per illuminant class or single

recommendation.note: No recommendation. The round trip and independent held-out absolute checks are both required by the agreed design.

decisions.blocks: Any absolute lux claim (rung 7).

decisions.title: Colour guardrails in mired
decisions.question: At which base CCT is today's kelvin guardrail translated, and do overlay looks get a colour guardrail?

options.label: Designer review (E11)
options.effect: New relative ranges set by design review.

recommendation.note: Translating at 2700 K preserves today's numbers at the look's base; any choice changes the old guardrail's meaning elsewhere, so it is the owner's.

decisions.blocks: Applying a learned colour offset (A10, A11).

decisions.title: Recording and retention
decisions.question: Which den sessions may be recorded and kept, who may appear, and are metering frames kept for gold sessions?

options.label: Decide explicitly
options.effect: Recording scope, retention, deletion and blurring stated before any session is kept.

parameters: metering frames or per-pixel maps for gold sessions

recommendation.note: No recommendation. Without retained frames, delivered service at R_eval is unknown.

decisions.blocks: The early need test (N1), delivered service at R_eval, and guest scoring.

decisions.title: Labelling and adjudication
decisions.question: Who labels, how disputes are settled, and is the worked patch marked on every need interval or a sample?

options.label: The owner alone
options.effect: Cheapest; no agreement measure.

options.label: Two blind reviewers and an adjudicator
options.effect: Agreement can be reported.

parameters: every interval or a sample (a sample narrows the service claim)
canary marking protocol and second blind pass

recommendation.note: No recommendation.

decisions.blocks: The gold set, R_eval coverage and canary service comparison.

decisions.title: Later learning permissions
decisions.question: May corrections ever train need or perception, may shared corrections update a household key, may device signals score, and is any appearance or identity allowed if geometry tracking fails?

options.label: Decide each explicitly
options.effect: Each permission is granted or refused on its own.

parameters: shared corrections updating the changer's household key
device signals (PC input) as scoring references
data use of crops, bundles and embeddings

recommendation.note: No approval is assumed for any of these.

decisions.blocks: Rung 12's unblocks, the student, any identity branch.

decisions.title: Physical capabilities and their qualification
decisions.question: Which engineered-fixture capabilities must be measured before any physical output, and is Hue mid-transition behaviour qualified?

options.label: Name the required measurements
options.effect: Inside the separate owner approval for physical output.

parameters: Hue landing on a command sent mid-transition

recommendation.note: All capabilities are unknown until commissioned. A9's 90°/s and 0.3 s settle are assumptions.

decisions.blocks: Any engineered physical output, E9, and gimbal admission.
